newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC did not discuss excess Brazil coffee exports.
newsitem.headline: ACPC did not discuss excess Brazil coffee exports.

text.p: Members of Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) did not last week discuss the possibility of Brazil exceeding its six million 60-kg bag export limit for January to June, a government official said.
"It was not discussed," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry, who has returned to Brazil from attending the meeting.
Based on information on May shipments contained in today's Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center bulletin, Brazil had exported 5.97 million bags of coffee from January to May 23.
According to today's bulletin, shipments based on bills of lading for May so far reach 847,372 bags.
Certificates of origin to May 23 had just slipped over one million bags while export registrations to May 16 were for 1.47 million bags to be shipped this month.
Registrations for June to the same date were around 900,000 bags, leading many traders to expect actual exports in the first half of this year in excess of seven million bags.
When asked if the government was prepared to take action should exports excessively overshoot the six million bag target, Assis said that he would have to have a meeting with exporters.
Many traders believe the government would be loathe to limit exports at a time when it is looking to minimalise a forecast large trade deficit in 1997.
At the ACPC council meeting in London last week, members decided to prolong the export quota accord for another twelve months to end-June 1998.

While the group decided on an overall limit for 1997/98 of 52.75 million bags, individual quotas would only be set at a meeting to be held in September, Assis said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
